title: BPXBATCH running a z/OS UNIX shell script: PARM with SH and a path, STDENV and STDPARM in-stream data sets
shapes: BDLD jcl/BDLDUT5.jcl BPX010: EXEC PGM=BPXBATCH,PARM='SH /u/bdld/bin/purge.sh 30', STDOUT and STDERR SYSOUT=*, STDENV DD * holding LANG and LC_ALL
BDLD jcl/BDLDUT5.jcl BPX020: EXEC PGM=BPXBATCH with no PARM, STDPARM DD * holding SH /u/bdld/bin/purge.sh AAAA continued by a second line BBBB
asserts: Each BPXBATCH step is a jcl_steps fact with program BPXBATCH (BPX010 with parm 'SH /u/bdld/bin/purge.sh 30', BPX020 with none) and an EXEC PGM call_sites fact that resolves to nothing in the estate and is no gap: BPXBATCH is system supplied. The path /u/bdld/bin/purge.sh is a z/OS UNIX file named in a shell command: not a dataset, not a program, no edge. STDOUT and STDERR are jcl_dds facts with sysout *. STDENV and STDPARM are jcl_dds facts with inline_lines 2; their lines are environment variables and parameter text, not utility control statements, so the steps have no jcl_utility_cards fact (the SH token and the continuation line BBBB are not verbs).

citations.doc: z/OS 3.1 z/OS UNIX System Services User's Guide (SA23-2279-60)
citations.quote: BPXBATCH is a utility that you can use to run shell commands or executable files through the batch facility.

citations.doc: z/OS 3.1 z/OS UNIX System Services User's Guide (SA23-2279-60)
citations.quote: In a batch job, BPXBATCH only allows up to 100 bytes for the parameter string due to JCL limitations.

citations.doc: z/OS 3.1 z/OS UNIX System Services User's Guide (SA23-2279-60)
citations.quote: To pass environment variables to BPXBATCH, you define a file containing the variable definitions and allocate it to the STDENV ddname.

citations.doc: z/OS 3.1 z/OS UNIX System Services User's Guide (SA23-2279-60)
citations.quote: If the STDPARM ddname is defined, BPXBATCH uses the data found in the specified file rather than what is found in the parameter string or in the STDIN ddname.

citations.doc: z/OS 3.1 z/OS UNIX System Services User's Guide (SA23-2279-60)
citations.quote: Records in in-stream data sets are concatenated with blanks as separator characters, and the string remaining after the SH token is passed as a single argument to a /bin/sh -c command.

citations.doc: z/OS 3.1 z/OS UNIX System Services User's Guide (SA23-2279-60)
citations.section: Guidelines for defining stdin, stdout, and stderr
citations.quote: It can be a sequential data set, a partitioned data set (PDS) member, a partitioned data set extended (PDSE) member, or SYSOUT.
